newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis wants EMU decision after March elections.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis wants EMU decision after March elections.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Wednesday that he wanted the decision on which countries qualify for European monetary union in 1999 to be taken after French parliamentary elections in March 1998.

"We must let the French elections go by," he told reporters ahead of talks in the central French city of Lyon with German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and central bank heads Jean-Claude Trichet and Hans Tietmeyer.
The European Commission has already suggested the likelihood is for the decision on EMU membership, which will be based on actual economic performances in 1997, to be taken in April 1998.

It reckons it will take until late February to have figures on actual fiscal and monetary performance in 1997, and then another six weeks or so to prepare European Commission and European Monetary Institute recommendations on which countries are ready for the single currency.
European Union finance ministers are due to discuss fixing a date for the decision on EMU membership at a meeting in the Netherlands next month.
